items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Mickey and I were the two drummers. We wound up playing fours.

ctx.x: Played with Bags [Milt Jackson] a lot too.

Underrated. All these guys are underrated. Mickey Roker. He’s a great player. We had a thing going on about Norman Granz’s Jazz at the Philharmonic. Mickey and I were the two drummers. We wound up playing fours. He made me stand up and take notice. Yes he did. Had the right attitude. Nice man. We had fun together.

You seem to be in the league, if not at the top drawer of the league, of people who, when somebody thinks of somebody who’s a nice person, as gentleman, as you’ve been described by both Duke Ellington and Jeff Castleman, as an angel, a saint. Has that worked against you in this business? You see all these abrasive people who make their reputation on being rough and tough, like Buddy Rich or Benny Goodman and other folks like that. Do you think it was a disadvantage? Do you think that works as a disadvantage, to…
